The statement’s tone is constructive and data-driven: it highlights strong real activity and labor-market gains with inflation near target and “balanced” risks, pairing a 25 bp hike and ongoing balance-sheet runoff with language consistent with a Taylor-like reaction function and the Taylor principle (the Fed “responds to inflation” and “follows [a] Taylor rule”). Stable long-term inflation expectations align with expectations-based Phillips curve frameworks (e.g., sticky-information models) and help limit inflation bias under a symmetric 2 percent objective. Strong labor conditions can tighten resource slack and gradually raise inflation pressures through labor-market frictions, while gradualism addresses real-time measurement risks emphasized in the literature. Normalization chiefly lifts short rates and can flatten the yield curve as expectations remain anchored. Overall, the sentiment is positive but measured rather than exuberant.
